newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Jan 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Jan 10.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
Experts predict the prices of agricultural products in domestic markets will drop gradually in 1997 if there are no big natural disasters.
Vice-premier and economic tsar Zhu Rongji says China must reform state enterprises this year, forcing through layoffs and bankruptcies to halt mounting losses.
A survey shows 13.9 percent of children aged 4-16 years have psychological problems.
President Jiang Zemin says China will not interfere in affairs to be handled by the Hong Kong government after the territory returns to mainland rule later this year.
China's tourism revenues reaches 240 billion yuan ($29 billion) in 1996. Foreign exchange earnings in the sector were $10 billion.
The demand for cement in 1997 is estimated to be 520 million tonnes.
China's tax revenue rises by 100 billion yuan ($12 billion) in 1996, a record increase.
